upstream: https://github.com/0xgoodcrypto/technocore-e2e
commit:   b71dd7634e85805ec53726d023bee87f5e8ab9e6
fetched:  2026-09-09T12:56Z
file:     e2e.py
sha256:   6a7419a6775a9f8cc48b086599382d9d8c22b896d009e7402e3743dbdd2aa1a4

WHAT THE STARTUP CHECK DOES

technocore_mcp compares vendor/e2e.py against the sha256 above at startup and
refuses to start if they differ. That detects local modification and corruption
of this distribution.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO

It does not detect that upstream has moved on, and it does not detect a value
replaced together with the copy -- both sides of the comparison live in this
directory. Upstream freshness is a separate check that compares the commit above
against upstream main; see docs/DESIGN.md section 4.

DO NOT EDIT vendor/e2e.py. It is a verbatim copy so that the upstream audit
results apply to these exact bytes. If it needs to change, the change belongs
upstream, and this file gets a new commit and a new sha256.
